title: Six healthy consumers, and the lag only goes up
intro: The email-sender consumers have fallen 2 million messages behind on the notifications topic and the gap is widening. All six pods of the deployment email-sender in namespace shop are Running with no restarts. CPU is low. Yesterday a change made each email include a rendered PDF receipt, which takes about a second per message. BS holds the bootstrap address; the consumer group is email-sender.

resolution: A Kafka consumer proves it's alive by calling poll() again within max.poll.interval.ms. These consumers fetched 500 messages per poll and had five minutes to finish them. That was easy when a message took a few milliseconds. Yesterday's change added a PDF to every email, about one second each, so a full batch took over eight minutes. Every consumer missed its deadline on every batch. Kafka's response is to assume the consumer has hung, remove it from the group, and reassign its partitions, which triggers a rebalance of the whole group. The removed consumer, still alive, finishes its batch, finds it can't commit its offsets because it no longer owns the partitions, and rejoins, causing another rebalance. The new owner starts the same messages again from the last committed offset. So the group spent its time reshuffling and reprocessing the same batches: pods Running, CPU low, lag climbing, and customers receiving the same email several times. The state told the story: a group that's never Stable is rebalancing, and the consumer's own log names the cause precisely. Fetching 100 messages per poll made each batch take about 100 seconds, well inside the deadline, and the group settled. The alternatives are raising max.poll.interval.ms, or better, making the work lighter: hand the slow part to a worker pool, or produce the PDF in a separate stage. The general rule: batch size times worst-case time per message must fit inside the poll interval, with margin, and any change that makes processing slower needs that sum redone. Monitor rebalance rate and time-since-last-poll, not only lag; and a cooperative assignment strategy keeps a rebalance from stopping the whole group.
